Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for the quick onboarding path you shared on the initial call. To keep procurement moving on our side, we need clarity on how Redwood will issue purchase references for our multi-SKU engagement. Attached is our completed onboarding form and a suggested line-item breakdown.

Specifically:
- Do you issue one master PO with internal line-item breakdown, or separate POs per SKU (we prefer separate POs to feed our internal cost centers)?
- Can spend caps be assigned per line item and enforced in your billing flow? We have a $120k cap on Platform Access (SKU: TXM-PLAT) and $35k on Enterprise Support (SKU: TXM-SUP).
- We also need the PO to reflect tax jurisdiction details; one line (professional services) should be flagged differently.

Attached: txm_vendor_onboarding_form.pdf; po_line_items_v2.xlsx (draft).

If you can confirm the expected PO numbering scheme and whether separate POs are possible, we can return a signed acceptance immediately.

Thanks,

Hi Elena — thanks for the packet and clear breakdown. Short answers up front: we can do either a single master PO with line items or separate POs per SKU; we typically issue separate PO references when customers request per-cost-center tracking, and we can enforce spend caps per PO.

A few clarifying questions before I generate the POs:
1) Do you want two distinct POs (TXM-PLAT and TXM-SUP) tied to your caps, or a single PO with two line items and a single cap?
2) Please confirm vendor legal name and tax ID exactly as it should appear on the PO (we need this for accounting).
3) Confirm whether the professional services line should be marked taxable — that changes the way we format the line description.

I’m looping in Marissa and Laura from procurement to help with the PO templates and internal approvals. If you’re good with separate POs, I’ll prepare draft PO numbers and send over DocuSign for signature.

Best,
